title: The Concept of Quantum Entanglement
text:
Quantum entanglement describes a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same fate, regardless of the physical distance separating them. When one entangled particle's state is measured (e.g., its spin), the corresponding state of the other particle instantaneously collapses into a correlated condition.

This immediate correlation puzzled Albert Einstein, who famously dismissed it as 'spooky action at a distance.' Mathematically and experimentally, entanglement proves that quantum mechanics cannot be fully explained by local realism—the idea that objects are only influenced by their immediate surroundings.

The primary implications of this concept lie in emerging technologies like quantum computing and quantum cryptography. Understanding how to maintain and utilize entangled states is key to building secure communication channels and exponentially faster processors.
